The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Mogannegowda, in the road traffic accident that took place on 31.10.2023.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 31.10.2023 at about 6.30 p.m., when deceased Mogannegowda(herein after called as deceased) was proceeding in motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-KB-5985, on near Govindanahalli circle, Kikeri Town, Channarayapattna to Mysore Road, K.R. Pet Taluk, Mandya District, at that time, the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-16-D-3565 came from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle, caused the accident and deceased Mogannagowda fell down and sustained fatal injuries and died on the way to hospital.

It is contended that,
post-mortem was conducted at K.R. Pet Government hospital and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards medical and funeral expenses.
3.
It is stated that the deceased was working as Agriculturist and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-16-D-3565.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1 and 2 have entered appearance through their learned counsels and filed their respective objection statements.

5. The 1st respondent in his objection statement denied all the averments made in the petition and contended that he is the owner of the vehicle bearing registration No. KA-16-D-3565 and was insured with the respondent No.2.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased and also the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.
It is admitted that the driver of Lorry was in possession of a valid driving licence at the time of accident.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, he has sought for dismissal of the petition.
6. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-16-D-3565 and contended that the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

It has denied the age,
income and occupation of the deceased and also the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

It has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-3565 was not holding valid driving license to drive the same as on the date of accident and hence, it is not liable to pay the Jayalakshmamma vs Srinivas on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70723581/
3 compensation.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

7. Based on the pleadings, this court has framed following issues:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 31.10.2023 at about 6.30 pm., when the deceased was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-KB-5985, near Govindanahalli Circle, Kikeri Town, Channarayapattna to Mysore Road, K.R. Pet Town, Mandya District, at that time driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-16-D-3565 came in rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the deceased vehicle, Due to the impact deceased was sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?
8.
In order to prove the case, 1 st petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and also examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 17 documents as per Ex.P1 to 17.
On the other hand, respondents have not led their defence evidence.
9. Heard the arguments.

10. My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3 ...

REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1 : It is the case of the petitioners that, on 31.10.2023 at about 6.30 p.m., when deceased Mogannegowda was proceeding in motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-KB-5985, on near Govindanahalli circle, Kikeri Town, Channarayapattna to Mysore Road, K.R. Pet Taluk, Mandya District, at that time, the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-3565 came from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle and caused the accident and deceased Mogannagowda was fell down and sustained fatal injuries and died on the way to hospital.

It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the offending vehicle driver and as such the respondents is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

12. In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.5 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R,

sentences.text: On the other hand, the version of the petitioners remains unchallenged and undisputed.
But mere unchallenged and undisputed facts does not amounts to proof of the same.
The petitioner is bestowed with the burden to prove the specific assertions in the light of oral and documentary proof.
14. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

15. According to the version of petitioners, the accident happened near Govindanahalli circle,
Kikkeri town, Channarayapattana to Mysuru road, K.R.Pete taluk and Mandya District, when the driver of Lorry came from opposite of the deceased's motor-vehicle with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased's motorcycle and caused the accident.

It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazar and Ex.P4 Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

On close Jayalakshmamma vs Srinivas on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70723581/
5 perusal of Ex.P3 and Ex.P4

it reflects that deceased was proceeding on his lane on the left side of the road and suddenly the offending vehicle came extreme right in opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to deceased's motorcycle.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
If the driver of Lorry vehicle coming in a normal speed by observing ongoing vehicle on his lane, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P.5 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P11 was also filed as against the driver of the offending vehicle.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P.11 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the Lorry vehicle driver.

16. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the driver of the Lorry is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the Lorry vehicle and he was charge sheeted.

17. Further though PW2 who is one of the eyewitness was cross examined by respondent counsel at length, nothing was elicited from his mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of deceased and on the other hand the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3 to P5 coupled with Ex.P11 clearly demonstrated that there is a negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-3565 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.2, I have already observed that the death of Mogannegowda, was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-16-D-3565.

6 19.
The petitioners have contended that the deceased was working as Agricultural/Coolie and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In order to prove the same, petitioners have not produced any documents before the court.

Therefore, considering the occupation of the deceased and year of the accident, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/-
per month.
20. It is stated that the deceased was aged years at the time of the accident.

The petitioners have produced the notarized copy of Voter ID Card of the deceased and also their family Ration card, in that ration card age of the deceased mentioned as 62 years, in Voter ID Card which shows the age as on 01.01.1994 is 30 years.
both documents are conflict to the age of the deceased, as per the Ex.P10 which was Post-Mortem report age of the deceased mentioned as 62 years.
The said document is scientific document, hence as per the Post-Mortem report the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 62 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '7'.
21.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
In the case on hand, deceased is aged above 62 years.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the deceased is not entitled to future prospects (as he was aged more than 60 years).
The deceased died leaving behind 5 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, th of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.12,000/- p.m.(Rs. 16,000 - Rs.4,000).
22. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.12,000/- p.m. and the multiplier '7' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.10,08,000/- (Rs.12,000X 12 X 7).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.10,08,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

23. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
24.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 and 5 are major children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Jayalakshmamma vs Srinivas on 6 January, 2026

7

Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 5 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.
An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their father.

Therefore, petitioner No.2 to 5 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
25.

In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.10,08,000/-
2. Towards loss of Consortium to Rs.48,400/- the petitioner No.1 3.
Towards loss to estate Rs.18,150/-

4. Towards transportation of dead Rs.18,150/-
 body funeral and obsequies  ceremony expenses  5. Towards loss of Filial Rs.1,93,600/-
 consortium to petitioner No.2 to  5(Each Rs.48,400/-)
 Total Rs.12,86,300/-

In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.12,86,300/-.
26.
As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the 1 st petitioner is the widow, petitioners No.2 to 5 are the minor children of the deceased.

Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No.1 to 5 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 60:10:10:10:10.
27.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondent No.2 has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

8 28.
Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-16-D-3565.
It is not in dispute that 1 st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle and 2 nd Respondent issued the policy in favour of the 1st Respondent.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.12,86,300/-(Rupees Twelve lakhs eighty six thousand three hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 60% Petitioner No.2 - 10% Petitioner No.3 - 10% Petitioner No.4 - 10% Petitioner No.5 - 10% Further it is ordered that, 25% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioners No.1 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years in her name and remaining 75% of the amount is ordered to be released in her favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share amount of Petitioners No.2 to 5 shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P.11 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the Lorry vehicle driver.
16. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.
Even in the instant case the driver of the Lorry is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the Lorry vehicle and he was charge sheeted.
17. Further though PW2 who is one of the eyewitness was cross examined by respondent counsel at length, nothing was elicited from his mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of deceased and on the other hand the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3 to P5 coupled with Ex.P11 clearly demonstrated that there is a negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
In this case, the petitioner No.2 and 5 are major children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Jayalakshmamma vs Srinivas on 6 January, 2026

22. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.12,000/- p.m. and the multiplier '7' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.10,08,000/- (Rs.12,000X 12 X 7).
Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.10,08,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
24.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 to 5 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
25.
In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.10,08,000/-
2. Towards loss of Consortium to Rs.48,400/- the petitioner No.1 3.
Towards loss to estate Rs.18,150/-
4. Towards transportation of dead Rs.18,150/-
 body funeral and obsequies  ceremony expenses  5. Towards loss of Filial Rs.1,93,600/-
 consortium to petitioner No.2 to  5(Each Rs.48,400/-)
 Total Rs.12,86,300/-
In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.12,86,300/-.
26.
Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No.1 to 5 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 60:10:10:10:10.
27.
Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.3:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.12,86,300/-(Rupees Twelve lakhs eighty six thousand three hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 60% Petitioner No.2 - 10% Petitioner No.3 - 10% Petitioner No.4 - 10% Petitioner No.5 - 10% Further it is ordered that, 25% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioners No.1 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years in her name and remaining 75% of the amount is ordered to be released in her favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share amount of Petitioners No.2 to 5 shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
